evidence.summary: Current main still gets MNP216 because process_run takes exactly one ProcessRequest.
Profile 0.18 process_run exposes bounded argv/env/stdin/output/deadline and exit status, but returns synchronously with no resource envelope or cancellation handle.
Forge handles unresolved/deferred obligations natively; this does not alter process_run capability.

metadata.pressure_boundary: synchronous process_run lacks aggregate resource envelope and source-visible in-flight cancellation handle

reproduction.instructions: Run tests/test_native_resource_policy.py::test_process_resource_handle_pressure_reproducer with mncs-language ff5e98c; expected MNP216 at process_run(request, envelope).

summary: The current main branch still reproduces the same narrow process-effect pressure after native status handling and defer/pending migration. ProcessRequest remains one typed request with synchronous ProcessResult; Forge native semantics can now choose resource budgets, admission, classification, pending and stale cancellation, but process_run still has no aggregate cgroup envelope or cancellable active handle.

workaround.description: Forge Runner retains Linux cgroup/systemd and process-tree realization after native decisions; the process effect contract remains an open language pressure.
